summary: CORRECTION (parent-derived, DOSBox-verified at Nate's direction) to the EQUIP wizard interaction model — our PORT had it backwards. The EQUIP per-slot picker's CURSOR starts on NONE (skip), not on the first candidate; the player moves the selection with UP/DOWN (cycling [NONE, candidate0, candidate1, ...], wrapping), and ENTER commits the cursored choice (NONE = leave the slot unequipped + advance; a candidate = equip it + advance). The 'arrow' (▸, glyph 0x64) drawn on an item is NOT the cursor — it is a static 'this item CAN be equipped in this slot' (candidate) marker. The CURSOR is a separate highlight: when on NONE, the prompt's 'NONE' is inverse-highlighted; when on a candidate item, that item's row is inverse-highlighted (boxed). An already-EQUIPPED item is shown with a CHECK glyph (0x17) instead of the ▸. Verified live in DOSBox: at slot-0 initial frame the cursor is on NONE (NONE highlighted) with ▸ on LONGSWORD; pressing DOWN moves the box onto LONGSWORD (NONE un-highlights); pressing DOWN again returns to NONE (1-candidate cycle is NONE<->item); pressing ENTER on a boxed LONGSWORD equips it (LONGSWORD now shows ✓) and advances to SECONDARY ITEM with the cursor back on NONE and ▸ on BUCKLER SHIELD. This SUPERSEDES wpcvw-equip-action.json's implied 'cursor starts on candidate 0 / LEFT-RIGHT nav / ▸ == cursor' reading and our port's implementation (initial cursor 0, LEFT/RIGHT, ▸ drawn at the cursor, prompt hardcoded NONE) — which made it impossible to tell you were selecting an item (up/down did nothing; the prompt always said NONE; pressing ENTER silently equipped candidate 0 instead of skipping).
method: Drove DOSBox-X (fresh boot -> build a 2-member party -> REVIEW MEMBER THESUS -> char view -> EQUIP) and observed the slot-0 then slot-1 frames, pressing DOWN/ENTER and screenshotting each. Saved two states and decoded the main-panel inventory-list cells via dump-cells.py --header 0x28,0x14,0x00,0x00,0x14 (40x20 @ (0,0) attr 0x14, cells +0x10): save 5 = slot-1 with LONGSWORD equipped + cursor on NONE; save 6 = slot-1 with the cursor boxed on BUCKLER. Committed engine fixtures equip-slot1-equipped + equip-slot1-selected (gen-fixture). Cross-ref the existing equip-slot0 fixture (slot-0 initial, cursor on NONE).

findings.claim: The EQUIP per-slot picker's cursor starts on NONE (the skip/empty position), NOT on the first candidate. The prompt 'SELECT <slot> > NONE' shows the COMMITTED value (NONE until you confirm), and the inverse-highlight on 'NONE' indicates the cursor is on NONE. The ▸ marker on a candidate item does NOT mean it is selected — only that it is equippable in this slot.

evidence.details: DOSBox: slot-0 initial frame shows the prompt 'SELECT PRIMARY WEAPON > NONE' with NONE inverse-highlighted (yellow) and ▸ on LONGSWORD. equip-slot0 fixture confirms. (Our port's cursor-0 render matched these PIXELS only coincidentally; the model differs.)

findings.claim: UP/DOWN move the selection, cycling through [NONE, candidate0, candidate1, ..., candidateN-1] and wrapping. DOWN from NONE -> candidate0; DOWN from the last candidate -> NONE. UP is the reverse. (With a single candidate the cycle is just NONE<->candidate0, verified: DOWN boxes LONGSWORD, DOWN again returns to NONE.) The candidates the cursor visits are ONLY the items equippable in the current slot — non-candidate items are never boxed.

evidence.details: DOSBox slot-0 (1 candidate): DOWN -> LONGSWORD boxed (NONE un-highlights); DOWN -> NONE highlighted again (LONGSWORD un-boxed). The cursor never lands on CUIRASS/LEGGING/SANDALS (non-candidates for the weapon slot).

findings.claim: The EQUIP inventory list draws each carried item with one of three presentations, decoded byte-exact from save 6 (slot-1, LONGSWORD equipped, BUCKLER cursored), main-panel rows 9-13, col 21 = marker, cols 22+ = name: (a) EQUIPPED item -> CHECK glyph 0x17 at col 21 attr 0x40, name attr 0x60 (LONGSWORD row: `17 40` then name bytes attr 0x60). (b) CURSORED candidate -> ▸ glyph 0x64 at col 21 attr 0x50, name attr 0x50 (inverse box) (BUCKLER row: `64 50` + name attr 0x50). (c) NON-cursored CANDIDATE -> ▸ 0x64 attr 0x50, name attr 0x40 (green) (LONGSWORD in the slot-0 initial frame, per equip-slot0). (d) NON-candidate, non-equipped item -> no marker (space at col 21 attr 0x40), name attr 0x90 (CUIRASS/LEGGING/SANDALS rows: `20 40` + name attr 0x90).

evidence.details: dump-cells save 6 main panel rows 9-13 cols 19-39: r9 (LONGSWORD equipped) col21=`1740` name=`4c60 4f60 4e60 4760 5360 5760 4f60 5260 4460` (attr 0x60) pad `2010`; r13 (BUCKLER cursored) col21=`6450` name=`4250 5550 4350 4b50 4c50 4550 5250 2050 5350 4850 4950 4550 4c50 4450` (attr 0x50); r10-12 (non-candidates) col21=`2040` name attr 0x90. FUN_8dcd (wpcvw 0x8dcd) is the per-row highlight renderer (equip-item-label-highlight-helper). The 0x17 check glyph / 0x64 arrow are font0 glyphs.

findings.claim: ENTER commits the cursored choice for the current slot and advances to the next populated slot: ENTER on NONE leaves the slot unequipped; ENTER on a candidate equips it (the item gains the ✓ marker, AC recomputes). Because committing advances, the prompt's NONE for a given slot is only ever replaced transiently — you don't see '> <item>' as a committed prompt for a slot you just left. The port must therefore: start the cursor on NONE, allow ENTER-on-NONE to skip the slot, and only equip when the cursor is on a candidate.

evidence.details: DOSBox: from slot-0 with LONGSWORD boxed, ENTER -> LONGSWORD shows ✓ (equipped) and the screen advances to 'SELECT SECONDARY ITEM > NONE' with cursor on NONE + ▸ on BUCKLER SHIELD.
